patch.value: Refusal recovery bundles echo URL credentials verbatim: attempted_command and normalized_args repeat a credentialed package source on stdout and in logs

Found 2026-11-08 during the CodeRabbit review of PR 1688. redactSensitiveCommandArgs (src/sdk/command-line.ts) redacts only history redact invocations. Every other refusal copies the raw argv into recovery.attempted_command and recovery.normalized_args, so a package source carrying URL credentials is repeated verbatim in the structured error on stdout, in CI logs and in any agent transcript. Reproduced with the built CLI and a fake credential. 'pm package install https://u:fake-secret@example.invalid/x.tgz --project --dry-run --bogus-flag --json' fails with unknown_option, and its attempted_command contains u:fake-secret. 'pm package --catalog --install <same> --output-limit 2' fails with read_output_mutation_conflict and shows the same echo. PR 1688 already withholds that refusal's executable retry for such an argv (pm-rrwh2o), so its recovery adds no further copy; the general echo predates that change. Telemetry already strips URL userinfo through stripUrlCredentials and redactUrlsInText in src/core/telemetry/policy.ts, but the CLI recovery path does not use them. Duplicate check: searched recovery attempted_command credentials url secret redact package source; pm-m0fh (closed) covered tracked files, not runtime refusal output.

Every CLI recovery representation (attempted_command, normalized_args, provided_fields, suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args) removes URL userinfo from every token, or withholds an executable retry when removing it would change the command's meaning; a spec drives an unknown_option refusal and a read_output_mutation_conflict refusal with a credentialed package source and asserts that no secret appears in stdout or stderr; history redact keeps its existing flag-value redaction
Refusal recovery output names a credentialed package source without its userinfo, and no secret appears in stdout or stderr
attempted_command and normalized_args repeat https://u:fake-secret@example.invalid/x.tgz verbatim for unknown_option and read_output_mutation_conflict refusals

value.text: Scope note from the PR 1688 Codex review: removing userinfo must cover every spelling the URL parser normalizes, not only the literal '//user:secret@'. A backslash authority behind a wrapper, such as npm:https:\user:secret@host, parses to the same credentials. pm-rrwh2o's carriesUrlCredentials, which parses each URL-scheme suffix with new URL, is the detection this item can reuse for redaction.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Correction to the earlier scope note: PR 1688 no longer ships carriesUrlCredentials. Four Codex rounds each found one more URL spelling the parser normalizes, so the retry guard became the conservative rule 'a token containing both @ and : may carry credentials'. For this item's redaction, which must rewrite tokens rather than withhold them, remove userinfo from a parse of a copy with tabs and newlines stripped, trying each scheme start. Where that cannot be proven, replace the whole token with a placeholder and drop the executable retry.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Implementation (branch fix/credential-shape-coverage): new src/core/shared/url-credentials.ts holds one conservative token rule: replace the span between a token's first ':' and its last '@' (after scheme slashes) with [redacted]. It is complete for every parser-normalized spelling for the same reason pm-rrwh2o's mayCarryUrlCredentials is. src/cli/runtime/refusal-credential-redaction.ts applies it once at emission, because many producers (unknown_option next_steps and examples, Commander retries recomputed at format time) echo the raw argv. It covers three paths: handleRunPmCliKnownError (context and message, before formatting, telemetry and Sentry), formatCommanderUsageJson (envelope, before lean projection and output-token accounting so the receipt measures the delivered bytes) and formatCommanderUsageMessage (text, before the help_format override). Each path replaces exact raw and both-shell-quoted spellings of every credential-bearing token and inline option value; this catches userinfo containing spaces. It applies the token rule to argv-token fields and the word rule to free text. When the retry text changes, suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args are withheld, and a next step tells the caller to restore the credentials. Verified with the built CLI: unknown_option (JSON and text), read_output_mutation_conflict (JSON and text), a space inside the password, a backslash authority and an inline --install= value all print zero secret bytes. Found while doing this: telemetry attempted_args leak userinfo whenever the host has no dot (filed pm-5htunt).

patch.value: The integration spec drives both refusals in both formats with zero secret bytes and no suggested_retry. A manual run of the built CLI also covers a space inside the password, a backslash authority and an inline --install= value. Unit specs cover withholding, shared and cyclic references, Windows and POSIX quoted spellings, envelopes and text (24 tests).

unknown_option and read_output_mutation_conflict refusals with a credentialed package source print no secret byte on stdout or stderr, in JSON or text, and expose no executable retry that would drop the credentials.

New core/shared/url-credentials.ts holds the conservative token rule (the span between the first ':' and the last '@'), exported through the SDK as redactUrlCredentialsInToken/redactUrlCredentialsInText/URL_CREDENTIAL_PLACEHOLDER. cli/runtime/refusal-credential-redaction.ts redacts typed refusals (main.ts, before formatting, accounting, telemetry and Sentry) and Commander usage errors (JSON before lean projection and output-token accounting, text before help_format). It replaces exact raw and shell-quoted spellings, applies the token rule to argv fields and the word rule to text, withholds a changed suggested_retry/suggested_retry_args, and adds a restore-credentials next step. history redact flag-value redaction is unchanged.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 1 on PR 1701 (head 5075d0757) found 7 issues. All were reproduced and fixed by a redesign rather than more spellings. (1) P1: replaceAll(raw, safe) interpreted a retained $& in the safe string; there is no string replacement of user-controlled text any more, and registry matching uses a replacer callback. (2) P1: bootstrap JSON help (maybeRenderBootstrapJsonHelp) built its unknown-command envelope from raw argv; it now builds from redacted tokens and passes the envelope pass. (3) P1: whitespace userinfo reached telemetry error text and Sentry pm.error_message; core/shared/url-credentials.ts now holds a bounded per-invocation registry (runPmCli registers it and resets it in finally) of whitespace-bearing userinfo spans plus both shells' escaping, matched case-insensitively by redactUrlCredentialsInText. That is the same rule telemetry, Sentry and the CLI use. Past 32 spellings it falls back to the provably complete whole-string rule. (4) P1: recovery command-name resolution lower-cased the token, and the spelling map was case-sensitive; every refusal builder (handleRunPmCliError context, resolveCommanderUsageContext, bootstrap help) now receives redactRefusalArgv(argv), so any transform it applies is safe by construction. (5) P2: buildLockConflictGuidance regenerated suggested_retry from the sanitized args after the pass; withholding now runs on the formatted envelope and applies whenever the invocation carried credentials, before lean projection and accounting. (6) P2 (secret rules) is recorded on pm-gh1699. (7) P2: spelling substitution was quadratic (16k args took 10 s); token fields get only the token rule and text gets one bounded regex, so the work is linear. A further leak was found during verification: telemetry command_taxonomy split an unknown-command token at whitespace. attemptedCommand now derives from the redacted argv. Queued-event reproduction: 0 secret bytes across 4 invocations.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: When refusal output echoes argv in transformed forms (lower-cased, truncated, re-quoted, split at whitespace), redact at the builders' INPUT, not at their output. An output-side pass only matches the spellings it enumerates, and every review round finds another. Give builders the redacted argv, keep a small registry only for what the word rule provably cannot reassemble (whitespace inside userinfo), and withhold executable retries on the FORMATTED envelope, because formatters regenerate them.

value.text: Codex review round 2 on PR 1701 (head 597b06b5a) found 6 issues, all reproduced. (1) P1: invalidExpectHash JSON-stringifies the value, so the registry now also holds each span's JSON-escaped spelling. (2) P1: concurrent in-process runPmCli calls clobbered the process-global registry; it now lives in an AsyncLocalStorage scope (runWithUrlCredentialInvocation), as expected-revisions.ts does, and a unit spec proves overlapping invocations stay apart. (3) P2: whitespace spans shorter than 4 characters ('x y') were skipped; the minimum is gone, since a whitespace-bearing span is at least 3 characters and specific to one invocation. (4) P2: the diagnostic budget was projected before my envelope pass changed the envelope, which left a stale receipt and 2,001 of 2,000 tokens. Redaction now happens once, on the guidance object that projectJsonErrorGuidance and renderBoundedGuidanceText both render, before the envelope, the budget and the accounting exist. The post-format wrappers in main.ts, commander-usage.ts and help-json-payload.ts are removed, and the repro now reports truncated: true with a consistent receipt. (5) and (6) are recorded on pm-gh1699.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 3 on PR 1701 (head 64ad09b5f): 2 P1 and 2 P2, all reproduced. (1) P1: parseExpectHashSpecs splits the value at its comma before echoing a fragment, so 'https://u:a b,rest@h' leaked 'https://u:a b' (a whitespace-free secret leaks the same way). This was the third spelling-class finding, so I replaced spelling registration with a rule whose bound can be proven. Each secret of the invocation (the password, or a bare token's whole userinfo; usernames are not secrets) is registered together with its shell and JSON escaping as a set of 6-character fragments. The text rule removes every run that shares a fragment, so any split, truncation, re-casing or partial escape exposes at most 5 consecutive secret characters. Six was chosen after 4 garbled ordinary guidance words ('Pass the', 'restore') for dictionary-like passwords. Shorter secrets containing whitespace are matched whole, and above 65,536 fragments the whole-string rule applies. (2) P1: formatPmCliErrorForDisplay's concise tracker-initialization branch rendered suggested_retry_args before the choke point; that function now redacts its guidance first. The restore step is excluded from redaction so a second pass cannot garble or duplicate it. Replayed 8 CLI reproductions with 0 leaks; 13 queued telemetry events had 0 leaks. (3) and (4) are on pm-gh1699.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 4 on PR 1701 (head 2f393c4a2): 1 P1 and 3 P2, all reproduced. (1) P1: producer diagnostics keyed by a source URL kept it, because only values were redacted. Object keys now pass the text rule as well, and a key that collides after redaction gets a numbered suffix. (2) P2: above 65,536 fragments the whole-string fallback could not see an @-less split echo. The fallback is gone. A longer secret is registered at aligned positions with stride ceil(positions / 65,536), each fragment at least stride wide. Consecutive matches still chain, so the leak bound degrades to fragmentLength + stride - 2 characters (5 for normal secrets) instead of failing open. Spellings are deduplicated before counting. (3) P2: userinfoBounds skipped every leading slash or backslash, which dropped a non-special scheme's backslash userinfo (git+ssh://\\\\...@h). It now skips at most the two authority delimiters, so extra delimiters are over-redacted, not missed. Recorded alongside: the fleet session's env-reference concatenation case went to pm-ycgb5g (flat grammar, out of this PR's scope).

value.text: Codex review round 5 on PR 1701 (head 8159f437b): 3 P1 and 1 P2, all reproduced. Two were regressions from round 4. (1) Token fields got only the token rule, so a token a producer cut before its @ (parseRegisteredItemFieldAssignments splits at '=') leaked; token fields now get the token rule and then the fragment rule. (2) The fixed-field exemption applied at any depth, so details.code echoed a credential. (3) Key redaction renamed host-owned schema keys, and a password 'required' renamed guidance.required and crashed the text renderer (ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE). For (2) and (3) the pass is now path-aware. Schema positions (the guidance and its recovery payload) keep their keys and fixed contract fields. Every other object is producer-owned: its keys and all of its strings are redacted. Specs drive formatPmCliErrorForDisplay and formatPmCliErrorForJson inside a credential scope for both reproductions.

value.text: Codex review round 6 on PR 1701 (head 5910631d6): 2 P2, both reproduced through the CLI. (1) Keys inside the recovery payload's typed descendants were renamed when a password's fragments matched them: a password containing 'comman' renamed recovery.fallback_candidates[].command. The pass now has three positions. Schema (guidance root and recovery) keeps keys and fixed fields. Typed (every other host-declared structure, such as candidates and side effects) keeps keys and redacts values. Producer (any details subtree) redacts keys and values. (2) Bounded text output could truncate the trailing restore warning for long URLs, so the restore step now comes first in next steps.

value.text: Hosted CI on 4b97c6a88: 14 of 15 jobs passed. Gates (coverage) failed at 99.99%. The uncovered code was all new branches: the lowerPreservingLength fallback (characters such as U+0130 whose lower case changes length), unterminated escaped literals, and the expect-hash placeholder arm, which only the uninstrumented built-CLI spec exercised. Unit specs now cover each one, and focused coverage puts url-credentials.ts and refusal-credential-redaction.ts at 100%. CodeRabbit (head 45c9d2daa): (1) Major. parseExpectHashSpecs echoed a 3-character piece cut before a comma ('https://u:abc'), which is inside the 5-character bound but still avoidable at the producer. When the argument carries userinfo, it now echoes such pieces only as the placeholder; no exported signature changes. (2) Minor. The Commander usage resolver read the tracker path from redacted argv, so C:\\Users\\a@b\\pm lost its custom-type guidance. It now parses bootstrap options from the unredacted normalized argv while guidance still uses redacted tokens. main.ts passes rawInvocationArgv to the resolver and formatters, which redact internally.
